taglines: It is Saturday which means the week is over but your brain did not get the memo and is still drafting responses to things that happened on Tuesday and scheduling follow-ups that will never be scheduled and running background processes from Wednesday at full CPU and the only way to stop it is to go outside and touch something that is not a screen.

You have a system and the system works but only when you use the system and you have not been using the system and instead you have been using a shadow system that is just the system but worse and less documented and held together by memory and hope and a sticky note that says 'important' with no further elaboration.

Someone somewhere is very confident about something that is not correct and they are sharing this confidence openly and people are nodding and you can see it but saying something would require a level of social investment that the situation does not quite justify and so you watch and nod slightly and carry it home and set it down and it is fine.

You are a sequence of decisions that mostly turned out okay and the ones that did not turn out okay produced information that was later useful and this is not a comforting thing to hear in real time but in retrospect it is the kind of thing you'd put on a wall if you were the type of person who puts things on walls which you are not.

Saturday has the energy of potential and the texture of Saturday and those two things are not always the same thing and learning to be at peace with the gap between them is either wisdom or resignation and honestly the distinction matters less than people claim.

Your phone has seventeen unread notifications and none of them are emergencies and two of them might be mildly interesting and the rest are the digital equivalent of someone clearing their throat in a room and waiting to be acknowledged and you are going to leave them on read and it is going to be fine.

The thing about coffee is that it works but it works differently at 9am than it does at 11am and by 2pm it is doing something entirely unrelated to alertness and you know this and you continue to operate the coffee timeline the same way every day because the alternative is thinking about it and thinking about it is exhausting.

Somewhere out there someone has it more figured out than you do and that is fine and normal and also that person has things that are less figured out than yours and is looking at someone else who seems further along and the whole thing is a long chain of people facing slightly ahead of themselves and nobody is at the front of it.
